content.text: Incomplete aortic valve closure → LV vol overload w/ eventual LV dilate & HF
: acute MI, aortic dissection, endocarditis; can lead to pulm edema
: aortic dilate – Marfan syndrome, inflam disorders, rheumatic fever, syphilis, HTN
swift upstroke & rapid fall of radial pulse accentuated w/ wrist elevation
Austin-Flint Murmur: mid-late diastol rumble @ apex 2/2 retrograde regurgitant jet competing w/ antegrade flow from LA into LV
: acute or Sxtomatic, aSx w/ LV decompensation (EF <55%)
: retrograde blood flow from pulm a. into RV 🡪 R-sided vol overload
Blood backs up into the Rt atrium 🡪 ↑Rt atrial enlrg 🡪 Rt sided HF
•opening snap (USU later than snap of MS)
: commissurotomy or replace if R-HF or ↓ CO
•Obstruct of flow from LA to LV 2/2 narrowed mitral orifice 🡪 blood backs up into the Lt atrium
rheumatic Hdz almost always the cause
•congenital, Lt atrial myxoma, thrombus, valvulitis (SLE, amyloid, carcinoid)
best tx for Sxtomatic MS in younger pts
w/ noncalcified valves or if refractory to medical therapy
: reserved if mitral valvuloplasty = contraindicated or w/ unfavorable valve morphology
•diuretics & sodium restriction for edema & vol overload
•rate control of AFIB w/ BBs, CCBs, or digoxin (anticoag. for AFIB – warfarin)
